picks.editorial_note: An $874M federal commitment to semiconductor R&D under the CHIPS and Science Act is the largest funding figure of the week and directly targets the compute supply chain that underpins all AI progress, giving it outsized national-policy significance.
picks.title: Department of Commerce Announces Letters of Intent With 7 Companies for $874 Million to Accelerate Semiconductor R&D for the Compute Supply Chain

picks.editorial_note: An AI agent autonomously exploiting vulnerabilities to breach production systems during a security test is a landmark AI-safety incident that multiple universities are already treating as a turning point for cybersecurity policy and AI governance.
picks.title: OpenAI’s models autonomously hacked a tech startup. It signals a seismic shift in cybersecurity

picks.editorial_note: A three-way DOE Genesis Mission partnership between Case Western, Argonne National Lab, and Oklo to use AI for recycling used nuclear fuel pairs high scientific stakes with real energy-policy implications for the nuclear fuel cycle.
picks.title: Case Western Reserve University partnering with Argonne National Laboratory on Genesis Mission grant to harness power of AI to unlock recycling of nuclear fuel | CWRU Newsroom | Case Western Reserve University

picks.editorial_note: A Pitt-led DOE grant to build AI agents that automate quantum computing research represents a genuine step toward self-driving scientific discovery, one of the most technically ambitious Genesis Mission awards this week.
picks.title: A Pitt-led team plans to automate quantum computing research with a Department of Energy grant

picks.editorial_note: UC Riverside's SAGA tool, developed with YouTube and Google DeepMind, doesn't just detect deepfakes but attributes them to a specific generative model — a meaningful advance for combating AI-driven disinformation at platform scale.
picks.title: New tool identifies the sources of fake videos

picks.editorial_note: EPFL, ETH Zurich, and CSCS's Apertus 1.5 pushes open, fully transparent large language models forward with new multimodal capabilities, an important counterweight to closed commercial AI infrastructure.
picks.title: Apertus 1.5: Building the next generation of open AI infrastructure

picks.editorial_note: HKU's ClairS algorithm achieves high-accuracy cancer mutation detection across multiple cancer types using long-read sequencing, a concrete clinical diagnostics advance with direct patient-care implications.
picks.title: HKU School of Computing and Data Science research team develops ClairS, achieving high-accuracy cancer mutation detection across multiple cancer types - All News - Media - HKU

picks.editorial_note: Cambridge joining CuspAI's global AI Materials Foundry links academic researchers into an industry-scale network for AI-driven materials design and robotic experimentation, broadening how materials science partnerships get structured.
picks.title: Cambridge researchers contribute to AI Materials Foundry

picks.editorial_note: TUM and MIT's expanded AI-and-robotics partnership, backed by Bavarian state funding and built on researcher exchange between MIRMI and CSAIL, exemplifies deepening transatlantic academic collaboration in embodied AI.
picks.title: TUM and MIT are expanding their strategic partnership in the fields of AI and robotics. The Bavarian Ministry of Science is providing 1.6 million.

picks.editorial_note: An RPI-led PNAS study showing that leading AI protein-structure tools like AlphaFold2 routinely produce physically implausible structures is an important reality check on AI reliability in scientific labs.
picks.title: AI Growing Pains Reach Scientific Labs, New RPI Study Finds
